transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-11 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Jared (Nebulon Head of ML), Priya (Platform Eng), Marcus (CTO)

Summary: quick pilot sync focused on tokens per dollar, microbench results since last week, caching gains observed on short prompts, and follow-ups to validate dedicated throughput. Some noisy audio, a couple speaker labels mismatch early on.

Topics: pilot metrics review, KV/prefix caching behavior, batching tradeoffs (latency vs tokens/sec/$), dedicated vs hosted pilot sizing, next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood): ok hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick agenda — numbers update, bench results, tuning recommendations, and who does what.
[00:12] Jared (Nebulon): yep thanks, we have about 45 minutes. excited to see the econom- the econ numbers.
[00:18] Diego (Redwood SE): cool, i'll start with the bench summary — since last week we ran the 8k context microbench on the r-infer- the rtx- style instances and also did an nvlink multi-gpu run. preliminary: tokens/sec per dollar improved about 22% when we enabled prefix KV caching for the FAQ style prompts.
[00:35] Priya (Nebulon): is that end-to-end including networking?
[00:40] Diego: yeah that's end-to-end within the test VPC, so includes serialization + grpc overhead. we saw median latency rise a hair for cold calls but amortized cost per token fell because of cache hits.
[00:55] Marcus (Nebulon): can you quantify "a hair"? our SLO is 200ms p95 for the chat use case.
[01:03] Diego: p95 cold was 380ms, warm after cache ~ 140ms; so warm meets the SLO, cold doesn't. but with a ~30% hit rate we move the overall p95 closer; the plan is to increase warm-up and pre-warm commonly accessed prefixes.
[01:20] Samira: quick note — we recommended using adaptive prefetching plus a small keep-alive pool to improve hit rates. that's in the config doc i sent last week.
[01:28] Jared: we saw batching helped tokens/sec/$ a lot but hurt latency. specifics?
[01:32] Diego: right. with synchronous single-request paths tokens/sec/$ baseline is X, batching up to 8x increased tokens/sec/$ by ~2.5x but added 80-120ms on average for tail latency. For your interactive chat flow that tradeoff is tricky; for backfill tasks or long-form generation it's a clear win.
[01:51] Priya: could we do hybrid? route short prompts with max-batch=1 and longer runs to batch pipeline?
[01:56] Lena (Redwood CSM): yes that's exactly the smart-routing pattern — route by length or by SLO tag, Redwood runtime supports policy based routing to different queues.
[02:07] Marcus: are there any cost math examples? tokens per dollar numbers?
[02:12] Samira: i updated the spreadsheet — short summary in chat: baseline model (redwood-curie-open) yields ~1.3k tokens per dollar for your median prompt length (280 tokens). With 4-bit quant and aggressive batching+cache we get to ~3.8k tokens per dollar in best-case. realistic pilot average we reported is ~2.5k tokens/$ due to mixed traffic and cold starts.
[02:36] Jared: 2.5k tokens/$ — how sensitive is that to a 2x increase in request rate?
[02:41] Diego: good question. tokens/$ is throughput/cost. when rate doubles you'll see improved utilization which raises tokens/sec and thus tokens/$ until you hit CPU/GPU saturation. If you hit per-GPU memory limits due to KV cache size you might need more instances which increases cost nonlinearly. we modeled a few scenarios in the spreadsheet.
[02:58] Priya: you mentioned KV cache memory pressure — how large is the cache per connection?
[03:03] Diego: depends on sequence length and keys — for your median session we measured ~60MB per active session with a 2k context warm prefix. when scaled to 500 concurrent sessions that becomes substantial. alternatives: store only smaller prefix windows or evict with LRU/preference heuristics.
[03:20] Jared: what were observed cache hit rates?
[03:23] Diego: in the FAQ-style traffic hit rates ranged 28-34% with prefix-only caching. if we do more aggressive prefix merging we think 40-50% is possible. that's what shaved off the ~22% cost improvement.
[03:36] (crosstalk) Speaker 1: so the warm vs cold is huge.
[03:40] Samira: yep, so practical suggestion — start with a hybrid routing policy: interactive route to low-latency queue (no batching, small kv-window), background jobs route to high-throughput queue (larger batch, full-kv).
[03:54] Marcus: dedicated vs hosted — we're leaning private for compliance. are there material econ differences?
[03:59] Diego: yes — Dedicated reserved capacity has lower per-token price at scale because you amortize GPU costs and can tune quantization/higher batch sizes more aggressively. Hosted is simpler and has burst capacity. For your pilot size (~200 rps peak) Dedicated on an annual reserved contract looked about 18-25% cheaper per token in our model, but requires upfront commit.
[04:20] Priya: any compliance blockers with hosted? we need audit logs, SSO, and KMS integration.
[04:25] Lena: Redwood hosted supports SSO/SAML, audit logs retention add-on, and customer-managed KMS for Private — we can provide the SOC2 sections and the KMS integration guide. i'll share links after the call.
[04:36] Jared: throw in the security docs pls.
[04:38] Samira: yes will do.
[04:40] Diego: back to perf — we tried a lightweight quant (4-bit) which reduced GPU memory 30% and increased batch capacity; perf was slightly slower on some ops vs 8-bit optimized kernels but cost wins outweighed. For your accuracy sensitive buckets maybe we keep 8-bit there and quantize lower priority routes.
[05:00] Priya: any visible regressions on generation quality? we have strict SOT of not hallucinating regulatory answers.
[05:06] Diego: in our evals we saw minor fluency differences mostly on long-form legal wording; for the regulatory route we suggested keeping the verified model (no quant) and adding reranker to validate answers, which adds compute but reduces risk.
[05:20] (short silence)
[05:24] Jared: ok let's talk benchmarking gaps — last week we asked for a 1h continuous run on a dedicated instance to simulate steady state; what's status?
[05:31] Diego: ran 45 min due to infra contention; saw throughput tail oscillations at 30 and 40 minutes likely due to garbage collection on the orchestration side. our ask: let us re-run with pinned kernel set and increased eviction thresholds.
[05:44] Priya: when you say orchestration GC, is that on your control plane or ours?
[05:49] Diego: our control plane test harness triggered a cleanup job; it shouldn't happen in your dedicated pilot. we'll make sure to disable it for the next run and provide logs.
[05:58] Marcus: do you have monitoring hooks we can plug to our prometheus?
[06:02] Lena: yes we offer metrics endpoints, traces, and log forwarding — we'll provide the mapping doc and a demo exporter; Samira will share that.
[06:10] Jared: anything about model fallbacks? we need graceful degradation if the big model saturates.
[06:15] Diego: yes that's built-in — policy-based fallback to a quantized variant or smaller model; you can set quality thresholds. we recommend soft-fallback first, then hard-fallback after x retries.
[06:27] Priya: on costs — can we do a one-week A/B to measure real tokens/$ in production?
[06:31] Samira: absolutely. propose a canary where 10% traffic routes to Redwood pilot with cache+batch policies for a week. we capture tokens, latency, and cost and compare to baseline.
[06:41] Marcus: are there any hidden costs — egress, logging retention etc?
[06:44] Samira: good call — egress if cross-region, logging retention beyond the free window is an add-on, longer KMS use has minimal per-token charges. we'll put an itemized line in the sheet.
[06:56] (noise on call)
[07:02] Diego: quickly on the spreadsheet scenarios — Scenario B assumed 40% cache hit, 4-bit quant for 60% of traffic, 2x batching for background jobs. that gets you to ~3.1k tokens/$ projected. Scenario A (conservative) kept 15% cache hit, no quant for regulatory paths and got ~1.9k tokens/$.
[07:22] Jared: ok that's helpful. what do you want us to validate this week?
[07:26] Samira: three asks: 1) Priya to spin up the dedicated test VPC and give access, 2) Diego to re-run the 1h bench with pinned kernels and full logs, 3) Samira to give updated spreadsheet and a one-week canary proposal for traffic routing.
[07:41] Priya: can do VPC by friday.
[07:44] Diego: i'll re-run and share logs by thursday.
[07:47] Samira: i'll send the spreadsheet & SOW draft by wednesday evening.
[07:51] Marcus: also please include a cost example for 3 month committed reserved vs monthly pay-as-you-go.
[07:57] Samira: noted, will include both and break out the delta per 1M tokens.
[08:03] Jared: last thing — will you give us a quick config snippet for the hybrid routing? we want something we can copy into our helm values.
[08:09] Diego: yes i'll attach a reference helm snippet in the slack thread.
[08:12] Lena: i'll also attach the security pack and the prometheus exporter config.
[08:16] (wrap-up) Samira: recap: action items in chat; next sync same time next week unless urgent. thanks everyone.
[08:25] Priya: thanks all.

End transcript.
